notes: Round 1, 21 Oct 2026. ACCESS LIMITS: every City of Vancouver host (vancouver.ca, guidelines/bylaws/council/syc/cd1-bylaws.vancouver.ca) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, and I did not try to bypass it. Those sources are therefore opened=false; their content is known only from search-engine summaries and is never marked 'verified' unless an opened page confirms it. Opened and usable: Shape Your City pages (review status, FAQ, Granville Street Plan), BC Laws (Vancouver Charter), Justice Laws (SOR/80-902), Transport Canada, Canada Gazette, NAV CANADA, CTBUH, Daily Hive, Storeys, Global News. The shared WebSearch quota ran out before I could search tower separation, floor-plate guidelines, the CAC policy and large-site rezoning policy; those gaps are flagged, not filled. KEY FINDINGS: (1) The VTC height band (244-305 m) lies wholly above the Higher Buildings Policy's published range (about 600-700 ft / 183-213 m), so every VTC tower is a departure to justify; the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded. (2) 'View Protection Guidelines' were replaced by Public Views Guidelines on 10 Jul 2024. (3) Transport Canada's July 2026 proposal to extend YVR zoning over much of Vancouver may affect downtown; surfaces are unpublished. (4) Bay Parkade (27 Jul 2026, 7-3) is the live precedent for a 288-315 m tower with an aviation height risk of about 27 m. TIME-CRITICAL: VTC registration closes 29 Oct 2026 and the Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026; submit the interpretation questions listed in flags (non-residential definition, height measure) before then. Team actions: download the Higher Buildings Policy, Public Views Guidelines and Downtown ODP by hand and verify the 'unverified' rows; request the Transport Canada detailed map (aviation.pac@tc.gc.ca). Shadow, energy and wind are pointers only (CLIM/ENER packets). The brief says its documents are academic, not legal.

modules.name: VTC hard-rules checker
modules.design_question: Does the massing satisfy the VTC hard rules (height band, 9.0 non-residential FSR, site limits, below-grade transit entrance), and which results depend on interpretation?
inputs: Layer0.Massing: tower and podium meshes with level planes
Layer0.ProgramTags: slab area by tag (from P01-M07 fsr_ledger)
Layer0.SitePolygon: 79.2 m x 144.8 m block and ground datum
Layer0.TransitConnection: tagged below-grade path or space reaching the station-side edge

parameters.name: Tower height H (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip)
parameters.relationship: Height up -> storey count up at fixed floor-to-floor. Pass only inside 244-305 m (800-1000 ft). The same height raises view-cone and aviation exposure (see P01-M04, P01-M05).

parameters.name: Counted non-residential floor area
parameters.relationship: Counted office and commercial area up -> non-residential FSR up in proportion. On the site of about 11,470 m2, 9.0 FSR needs about 103,200 m2 (derived arithmetic, not a brief figure).

parameters.name: Site coverage of above-grade volume
parameters.relationship: Coverage up -> fewer storeys for the same area but less open ground for public realm. All above-grade volume must stay inside the 79.2 x 144.8 m block.

parameters.name: Below-grade transit connection continuity
parameters.relationship: A continuous below-grade path from the building to the station-side edge meets 'connecting directly'. Path length up -> walking time and wayfinding burden up (MOBI packet).

parameters.name: Level bands holding public-tagged area
parameters.relationship: More level bands with public-tagged area -> closer to 'public-facing uses extend vertically'. The brief says 'should', so this is a soft rule.

parameters.name: Interpretation switches (height measure; all towers vs at least one; which uses count as non-residential)
parameters.relationship: Each switch moves pass/fail without moving the design, so each is logged as an assumption until Buildner answers (Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026).

metrics.name: Tower height band
metrics.good: 244-305 m for every tower (strict default)
metrics.bad: below 244 m or above 305 m for any tower
metrics.method: H_arch measured from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance (CTBUH architectural top, antennae excluded); H_occ and H_tip also reported.
metrics.basis: Brief band 800-1000 ft; CTBUH height definitions. Brief extract supplied by the project; PDF is gated.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, strict (office + commercial)
metrics.method: Sum office and retail/commercial slab area / site area.
metrics.basis: Brief minimum 9.0 non-residential, high-employment floor area.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, broad (adds hotel, cultural/civic, public)
metrics.good: strict value already >= 9.0 (no interpretation needed)
metrics.bad: broad value < 9.0 (fails under every reading); strict < 9.0 <= broad is amber 'needs interpretation'
metrics.method: Same ledger with a wider tag set.
metrics.basis: Brief wording 'office, commercial' leaves hotel and civic uses undefined; see flags.

metrics.name: Site boundary containment
metrics.good: all above-grade volume inside the polygon of about 11,470 m2 (tolerance editable, default 0.1 m)
metrics.bad: any above-grade volume outside the polygon
metrics.method: Extruded-polygon containment test on the massing.
metrics.basis: Brief site size 79.2 x 144.8 m (approx.). Tolerance is a team setting.

metrics.name: Below-grade secondary transit entrance
metrics.good: tagged below-grade connection present, continuous, touching the station-side boundary
metrics.method: Graph path from a core node to the boundary segment facing the station.
metrics.basis: Brief requires a below-grade secondary entrance connecting directly to the neighbouring station.

metrics.name: Vertical presence of public uses
metrics.good: >= 3 bands (base, mid, upper) contain public-tagged area
metrics.method: Count distinct level bands with public, cultural/civic or amenity tags.
metrics.basis: Team preset (editable); brief only says 'should extend vertically'.

modules.method: 1) Read the site polygon and compute its area (Shapely). 2) For each tower solid find top Z and the Z of the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance; output H_arch, H_occ, H_tip. 3) Sum slab areas by tag from P01-M07; FSR = area / site area; run strict and broad classifications. 4) Test that all above-grade mesh lies inside the site polygon within tolerance. 5) Build a graph of tagged below-grade spaces and test for a path from a core node to the station-side edge segment. 6) Count level bands carrying public tags. 7) Emit one rule record per check with value, threshold, state (pass / fail / needs interpretation), the interpretation switches used and the source id. No rule silently passes: missing tags give 'unknown'.
visualization: Row of badges (green pass, red fail, amber needs interpretation, grey unknown), each linked to the brief clause and source id
Elevation silhouette of each tower on a metre ruler with the 244-305 m band shaded and 800/1000 ft ticks
FSR gauge 0-12 with a vertical line at 9.0 and two markers (strict, broad)
Plan view: site rectangle 79.2 x 144.8 m, tower footprints, below-grade transit path as dashed line
outputs: compliance_report: list of {rule_id, value, threshold, state, source_id}
tower_heights: three heights per tower, m
modules.human_judgment: Reading ambiguous brief wording (uses counted as non-residential, height measure, all towers or one); deciding to breach a rule on purpose and arguing it; asking Buildner before 3 Nov 2026.
modules.limits: The full brief PDF is email-gated, so rules come from the team's extract. The checker tests geometry and tags, not design quality. The brief is not a legal document and the jury may reward justified breaches, so failures are flags, not disqualifications. Station portal location must be tagged by the user.

libraries.name: json-rules-engine
libraries.role: Rules as editable JSON with source ids

modules.name: Policy stack register and departure log
modules.effort: S: about 3 person-days, plus monthly register updates
modules.design_question: Which Vancouver policies govern a tall tower here, what is each one's current status, and where does the design knowingly depart from them and why?
inputs: Static policy register (JSON): document, version, date, status, URL, clause
Rule results from P01-M01, P01-M03, P01-M04, P01-M05, P01-M06
User departure notes: free text plus evidence source ids

parameters.name: Policy status and version date
parameters.relationship: Newer or under-review documents change which clause applies. Draft policies are due fall 2026-winter 2027 and the hearing spring 2027, so every result stays 'provisional' until then.

parameters.name: Membership of the Higher Buildings policy area
parameters.relationship: Inside the area, buildings up to 600 ft may be considered through the Higher Buildings review. Outside, Council's 2023 direction sends non-conforming schemes through rezoning judged on their own merits.

parameters.name: Proposed height relative to policy range
parameters.relationship: Height up beyond about 600-700 ft (183-213 m) -> larger departure from the policy. The VTC band 244-305 m lies wholly above that, so every VTC tower is a departure to justify.

parameters.name: Review process and design-excellence evidence
parameters.relationship: Higher Buildings sites get an enhanced review with Urban Design Panel and Council approval; more ambitious height -> more design-excellence evidence expected (summaries of older versions, unopened).

parameters.name: Written departure rationale
parameters.relationship: A sourced rationale per departure turns a breach into an argument. The brief states the jury may reward justified breaches.

parameters.name: Precedent register (Bay Parkade rezoning, 27 Jul 2026, 7-3)
parameters.relationship: Council accepted three towers above policy heights through rezoning with a large benefits package. It is evidence of a path, not a rule.

metrics.name: Height inside 'may be considered' range for policy-area sites
metrics.method: Compare each tower's H_arch with 600 ft.
metrics.basis: City FAQ: sites inside the policy area, buildings up to 600 ft may be considered.

metrics.name: Height vs tallest CBD range quoted from the policy text
metrics.good: <= about 700 ft (213 m)
metrics.bad: > about 700 ft (213 m): all of the VTC band
metrics.method: Same comparison against the 550-700 ft range.
metrics.basis: Search summaries of the 2011 and 2018 policy versions; PDFs not opened.

metrics.name: Departure log completeness
metrics.good: 100% of departures have rationale, evidence id and jury tag
metrics.method: Count complete records / total.
metrics.basis: Course rule that every result cites its source (team preset).

metrics.name: Register freshness
metrics.good: <= 14 days before 30 Nov 2026 (editable)
metrics.method: Date stamp per register row.
metrics.basis: Team preset: review drafts and Bay Parkade follow-ups are moving targets.

modules.method: Load the register with one row per document (Higher Buildings Policy with its 1997/2003/2011/2018 versions, Public Views Guidelines July 2024, Downtown ODP, Granville Street Plan June 2025, Higher Buildings Policy Review phases, Bay Parkade precedent). For each module result, link the governing clause and status. Compute height deltas against 600 ft and about 700 ft. For every fail or amber result require a departure record (clause, design value, policy value, delta, rationale, evidence ids, jury tag). Rows from superseded documents or later-corrected claims stay visible with a FALSE ASSUMPTION colour. Export the register and departures as markdown for the 'policy reflection' deliverable. The tool never writes the rationale.
visualization: Horizontal timeline 1997 > 2003 > 2011 > 2018 > Jul 2024 Public Views Guidelines > Jun 2025 Granville Street Plan > 2026 review phases > spring 2027 hearing, coloured in force / amended / under review / superseded
Clause table with pass, depart, n.a. badges linked to source ids
Height ladder in metres: 183 m (600 ft), 213 m (700 ft), VTC band 244-305 m, each tower as a marker
FALSE ASSUMPTION rows in a fixed magenta that stays on screen
outputs: policy_register: list of {doc, version, date, status, url}
departure_register: list of {clause, design_value, policy_value, delta, rationale, evidence_ids, jury_tag}
policy_reflection_text: markdown for the PRES boards
modules.human_judgment: Whether and why to depart; reading policy intent (architectural excellence, skyline contribution); relating the scheme to cultural and Indigenous perspectives. All policy-reflection writing stays human.
modules.limits: City policy PDFs returned HTTP 403, so clause text, the 1997 adoption date (22 Apr vs 6 May in different summaries) and the Figure 1 site list are unconfirmed. Draft policy from the 2026 review is not public until early 2027. The brief says its documents are academic, not legal.

libraries.name: json-rules-engine
libraries.role: Register rows and rule links as JSON

libraries.name: Claude skill anthropic-skills:docx / anthropic-skills:xlsx
libraries.role: Export departure log and reflection text

modules.name: Zoning and Downtown ODP data sheet
modules.design_question: What do the Downtown ODP and CBD zoning set for land use, density, height, parking and loading here, and which rules can be relaxed or replaced by CD-1 rezoning?
inputs: Layer0.SitePolygon with assumed block location and ODP sub-area (team assumption: CBD)
gfa_by_tag and FSR from P01-M07
Tower heights from P01-M01
Parking and loading counts from Layer 0 tags or ADVANCED presets (MOBI/SYST packets)

parameters.name: ODP sub-area / district
parameters.relationship: The sub-area selects the permitted uses and the FSR minimum and maximum. The VTC block is hypothetical, so the sub-area is an assumption that moves every cap below.

parameters.name: Maximum FSR
parameters.relationship: Cap up -> permitted floor area up. Above the cap, density must come through bonus or CD-1 rezoning (press reports Bay Parkade consolidated at 27.4 FSR).

parameters.name: Minimum FSR / required use
parameters.relationship: The ODP sets minimum density standards. A higher employment minimum -> more office area and fewer residential floors. VTC's 9.0 non-residential minimum is a separate brief rule.

parameters.name: Height (interpretive provision)
parameters.relationship: ODP height provisions are interpretive and can be varied in design and approval, so zoning does not cap a supertall. The practical caps are view cones, aviation and rezoning negotiation.

parameters.name: Relaxation by the Development Permit Board
parameters.relationship: Relaxation is available where literal enforcement causes unnecessary hardship; larger departures push the scheme toward a CD-1 rezoning.

parameters.name: Parking cap and loading minimum
parameters.relationship: Parking cap down -> fewer below-grade levels. Loading minimum up -> more service bays on lane frontage, less active frontage (geometry; see MOBI and PUBL packets).

parameters.name: Zoning path (outright, relaxation, CD-1)
parameters.relationship: A CD-1 sets site-specific height, FSR and conditions; Bay Parkade's sets only a maximum height. The path sets the scale of the benefits negotiation in P01-M08.

metrics.name: Total FSR vs ODP maximum
metrics.good: <= district maximum typed in from the ODP (value not read in this run)
metrics.bad: > maximum with no stated bonus or CD-1 path
metrics.method: Compare M07 total FSR with the entered cap.
metrics.basis: ODP summary only; PDF unopened.

metrics.name: FSR vs ODP minimum / use mix
metrics.good: >= entered minimum
metrics.method: Compare use-based area with the entered minimum.
metrics.basis: ODP summary only.

metrics.name: Parking and loading counts
metrics.good: within entered cap and at or above entered minimum
metrics.method: Counts from Layer 0 tags.
metrics.basis: ODP summary only; numbers not read.

metrics.name: Zoning path declared
metrics.good: scheme names its path (outright, relaxation or CD-1) and cites the clause
metrics.method: Required field in the sheet.
metrics.basis: Bay Parkade went through CD-1 rezoning outside the policy area; Council 2023 direction.

modules.method: Keep a data sheet where each row is {parameter, value, source clause, status}. Rows are filled by hand from the Downtown ODP and District Schedule PDFs; the tool never guesses a value. Compute design values from Layer 0 and P01-M07, compare with the entered caps and mark each row: within / needs relaxation / needs CD-1 / unknown. Unknown rows become editable team-assumption cells in a distinct colour; when a value is later corrected, the old row stays visible with a strike-through and the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour. Output a zoning_envelope object for downstream modules.
visualization: Data-sheet table with chips: within (green), needs relaxation (amber), needs CD-1 (red), unknown (grey hatched)
Bars of design FSR against cap; the cap bar is hatched until a value is entered
Plan strip showing parking and loading counts against limits
outputs: zoning_envelope: {sub_area, fsr_max, fsr_min, height_note, parking_cap, loading_min, path, source_ids, status}
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the zoning path and arguing relaxation; picking the real block assumed for the hypothetical site; confirming the current ODP consolidation with City planning.
modules.limits: The ODP PDF was blocked (HTTP 403); only a search summary (land use, FSR min/max, parking caps, loading minimums, interpretive height, relaxation power) was available, so no FSR, parking or loading numbers are given. The site is hypothetical. District schedule, CBD guidelines and CD-1 precedents must be read by the team.

libraries.name: json-rules-engine
libraries.role: Cap and minimum rules from the data sheet

libraries.name: GeoPandas
libraries.role: Optional zoning polygons from City open data

modules.name: Public view-cone checker
modules.effort: L: about 8-12 person-days (manual-parameter mode about 3 days is core; open-data ingestion 5-8 days is v1)
modules.design_question: Does the massing penetrate a protected public view cone from Queen Elizabeth Park or other origins, by how much, and does that trigger a Higher Buildings special review?
inputs: Layer0.Massing in a projected CRS with geodetic Z
Site georeference, ground elevation and vertical datum (team assumption until a real block is chosen)
View-cone data: origin point, left and right bounds, lower boundary (maximum geodetic height), view subject
Context massing (existing and approved towers), optional

parameters.name: Cone lower-boundary elevation at the site
parameters.relationship: Cone floor up -> allowable top up; allowable height = cone elevation - ground elevation. Older documents suggest floors near 100-145 m for downtown sites, far below 244-305 m (derived, unverified).

parameters.name: Footprint position relative to cone bounds
parameters.relationship: Footprint outside the left and right bounds -> no penetration at any height. Inside the wedge, every metre above the cone floor is penetration.

parameters.name: View origin point and subject
parameters.relationship: The origin is the camera for the skyline view and fixes what is tested; moving it changes every result. The brief requires one skyline view from the Queen Elizabeth Park viewpoint.

parameters.name: Cone vintage
parameters.relationship: After 10 Jul 2024: 38 cones cut to 24, view 3.1 removed, 3.2.1-3.2.4 retained. Pre-2024 data overstates restriction and misplaces tests.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings site status
parameters.relationship: Only select downtown Higher Buildings sites may enter Queen Elizabeth Park cone boundaries, via a special review. Elsewhere penetration is not an option. The 2026 review does not revise protected views.

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> allowable height above grade down for a fixed cone floor (arithmetic).

parameters.name: Angular width of the tower from the origin
parameters.relationship: Width up -> more of the view subject (mountain skyline) covered. No sourced acceptable-occlusion threshold found (see unresolved relationships).

metrics.name: Maximum penetration per cone
metrics.good: 0 m (all parts outside the cone)
metrics.method: Max over mesh vertices and subdivided edges of (z - cone floor).
metrics.basis: Search summary of the Public Views Guidelines: all parts of a building should lie outside cone boundaries. PDF unopened.

metrics.name: Higher Buildings review trigger
metrics.good: no penetration, or penetration only at an identified Higher Buildings site with review planned
metrics.bad: penetration at a site not in the policy area
metrics.method: Penetration > 0 AND site-in-policy-area flag from P01-M02.
metrics.basis: City page summary of the special review process; policy area map unopened.

metrics.name: Cone dataset vintage
metrics.good: post-10 Jul 2024 Public Views Guidelines geometry
metrics.bad: pre-2024 View Protection Guidelines data (38 cones)
metrics.method: Check dataset date stamp; warn on 2015 or 2020 archive snapshots.
metrics.basis: Council replaced the View Protection Guidelines on 10 Jul 2024.

metrics.name: Occlusion of the mountain skyline from the origin
metrics.good: 0% (team target)
metrics.bad: any occlusion; severity judged by people
metrics.method: Ray grid from origin through the cone window; share of rays hitting the massing before the subject.
metrics.basis: Team preset; no sourced threshold.

modules.method: Convert site and massing to the City's coordinate system and vertical datum (confirm the datum first). Build each cone as a wedge: origin point, two azimuth bounds and a lower surface from the cone's geodetic elevation data. For every mesh vertex and subdivided edge inside the wedge compute margin = z - cone_floor(distance, azimuth); penetration = max margin. Cast a grid of rays from the origin through the cone window toward the view subject (three-mesh-bvh) and count hits on massing and on context towers. Render the origin-point view with the cone window and silhouettes. Manual mode: the user types cone floor elevations and azimuths copied from a City View Cone Assessment. Open-data mode loads the City view-cone dataset and shows its date.
visualization: Plan: wedge cones in translucent colour, origin point, azimuth bounds, site outline
Section along the cone axis: cone floor line, tower, penetrating part in red
Origin-point panorama: cone window outline, mountain subject, tower silhouette against context towers (also feeds the PRES skyline view)
False-colour on the tower mesh: green below the cone to red above, legend 0-200 m penetration
outputs: view_cone_report: list per cone {cone_id, penetration_m, margin_m, source_id}
modules.human_judgment: Whether penetration is justified; judging skyline silhouette and the 'City in Nature' relationship; requesting an official View Cone Assessment for a real parcel; moving towers to avoid cones.
modules.limits: The Public Views Guidelines PDF and VanMap data could not be opened (HTTP 403), so cone geometry is user-supplied. Cone elevations quoted in this packet come from older council documents and are not current. The block is hypothetical, so cones apply only after an assumed real location and datum.

libraries.name: trimesh
libraries.role: Mesh clipping and ray queries (manifold3d for booleans)

libraries.name: three-mesh-bvh
libraries.role: Fast raycast against massing in the browser

libraries.role: CRS transforms (vertical datum grids not confirmed)

modules.name: Airspace height screening
modules.design_question: Could federal aviation rules (YVR zoning, NAV CANADA procedures, harbour heliport and floatplane surfaces) cap or force changes to tower height, and what must the team submit or ask?
inputs: Tower top elevation (m above sea level) and footprints from Layer 0
Site latitude/longitude (assumed block)
Optional heliport FATO position, approach azimuth, number of paths, performance class
Optional user-supplied Transport Canada map or surface heights; crane height assumption

parameters.name: Tower top elevation
parameters.relationship: Top up -> more likely to penetrate an obstacle surface or instrument procedure. At Bay Parkade, NAV CANADA review may trim the 315 m tower by about 27 m (88 ft).

parameters.name: Distance and bearing to runway strips
parameters.relationship: Under SOR/80-902 approach surfaces rise 1 m per 50 m out to 15 km, so allowable height grows with distance along the approach. Outside the regulation's outer limits it does not apply.

parameters.name: Outer-surface plane
parameters.relationship: A plane 45 m above the airport reference point (reference elevation 2 m) caps heights inside the outer limits, which the regulation describes mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary.

parameters.name: Proposed 2026 zoning extension
parameters.relationship: Transport Canada proposes new height limits over much of Vancouver north of the Fraser. If the CBD is inside, a new surface caps new towers and taller existing buildings become non-conforming. Heights unpublished.

parameters.name: Heliport approach and transitional surfaces
parameters.relationship: Standard 325 non-instrument surfaces climb 6-10% for 245 m, then 16% for 830 m, with 50% transitional slopes to 45 m; closer to the path -> lower allowable height. H1 heliports use a critical-obstacle line instead.

parameters.name: NAV CANADA assessment timing
parameters.relationship: Review covers line of sight, flight paths, interference and light; usual reply 8-12 weeks, 12-18 months near airports. The letter is not a permit, so a late request can force floor cuts.

parameters.name: Temporary crane top
parameters.relationship: Crane top above tower top -> separate aviation concern; YVR raised crane concerns at Oakridge, per the Bay Parkade architect.

metrics.name: YVR zoning surface penetration
metrics.good: <= 0 m, or site outside the outer limits
metrics.method: Tower top minus approach/outer/transitional surface height at each footprint vertex.
metrics.basis: SOR/80-902 s.5 and surface formulas; downtown applicability unconfirmed, so result may be 'unknown'.

metrics.name: Heliport surface penetration
metrics.good: <= 0 m against Standard 325 surfaces for the entered FATO
metrics.method: Surfaces from Table 4-1 values for the entered path count and class.
metrics.basis: Standard 325 table values; heliport certification and class unknown.

metrics.name: Precedent screening flag
metrics.method: Flag only; not a rule.
metrics.basis: Bay Parkade's tallest tower would reach 288 m after a possible full NAV CANADA reduction; site-specific, editable.

metrics.name: NAV CANADA lead time
metrics.good: assessment requested at pre-design (8-12 weeks typical)
metrics.bad: requested after design freeze (12-18 months near airports)
metrics.method: Checklist date logged by user.
metrics.basis: NAV CANADA land use page.

modules.method: Transform tower footprints and tops to latitude, longitude and metres above sea level. Build YVR surfaces as a heightfield: approach (1:50 plane, 15% divergence each side, to 15 km at the tabulated end heights), outer (47 m AMSL, from 45 m above the 2 m reference), transitional (1:7 up to 45 m above the reference). For a heliport, build the Standard 325 Table 4-1 surfaces from the user's FATO position, azimuth, path count and class. Penetration = tower top - surface height at each footprint vertex. Return pass, fail or unknown; unknown whenever a surface or outer limit is missing. Add the precedent flag and a checklist: NAV CANADA portal submission, Transport Canada detailed-map request (aviation.pac@tc.gc.ca), crane assumptions. The module never reports 'approved'.
visualization: 3D translucent surfaces with the tower; penetrating mesh in red, legend 0-30 m
Chart of allowable height against distance along the approach with the tower top as a marker
Status cards: pass (green), fail (red), UNKNOWN (grey hatched, never green)
outputs: airspace_flags: {yvr_zoning, proposed_2026_zoning, heliport, nav_canada} each pass / fail / unknown
modules.human_judgment: Engaging NAV CANADA and Transport Canada; deciding to trim floors or reposition; assessing helicopter and floatplane routes and obstruction lighting. No output is an aviation approval.
modules.limits: Downtown applicability of every surface is unconfirmed. The 2026 proposal's surface heights are unpublished (consultation closed 12 Sep 2026). Instrument flight procedures, harbour water-aerodrome data and heliport certification were not found. Obstruction marking and lighting rules were not researched. Screening only.

modules.name: Tower siting, separation and floor plate
modules.design_question: Do tower positions, floor plates and separations from on-site and neighbouring existing or approved towers meet downtown guidelines, and which departures need justification?
inputs: Layer0.Towers: floor-plate polygon per level
Layer0.Podium and site edges (streets, lanes)
Context massing tagged existing or approved-not-built
Grid-to-true-north offset typed from the site plan

parameters.name: Tower-to-tower separation above podium
parameters.relationship: Separation up -> daylight, privacy and sky view up, usable footprint down. A downtown value of 24.4 m (80 ft) is recalled but unverified. The brief asks entrants to consider tower spacing.

parameters.name: Floor-plate area and width by level
parameters.relationship: Plate width up -> shadow width and wind-facing width up (geometry; quantified in CLIM packets) and slenderness down. No downtown floor-plate cap was verified.

parameters.name: Setback to lot lines and lanes
parameters.relationship: Setback up -> public realm and lane width up, floor-plate area down.

parameters.name: Distance to approved-not-built towers
parameters.relationship: Closer approved towers in the same height range -> separation shrinks and needs negotiation; context must include approved towers such as Bay Parkade.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north offset
parameters.relationship: Offset decides which facade faces which compass direction in sun, wind and energy modules. The brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid; the value is not known here.

metrics.name: Minimum tower-to-tower separation per level band
metrics.good: >= 24.4 m (80 ft) (candidate, editable)
metrics.method: Minimum polygon distance and facade-normal distance per band above podium.
metrics.basis: Recalled downtown-guideline value; no City guideline could be opened.

metrics.name: Floor-plate area band
metrics.good: inside the team-entered band (no default supplied)
metrics.method: Area per level from slab polygons.
metrics.basis: No sourced downtown floor-plate cap found; band is a team setting.

metrics.name: Context completeness
metrics.good: all existing and approved towers within the review radius (editable) are in the model
metrics.method: Compare context list with the City's approved-tower register.
metrics.basis: Brief context includes existing high-rises and approved towers.

modules.method: Slice each tower into level bands above the podium (Shapely). For every tower pair, on-site and context, compute the minimum polygon-to-polygon distance and, for facing facades, the perpendicular distance along facade normals; keep the minimum per band. Compute floor-plate area, perimeter and bounding width per level. Compute each facade's grid and true-north bearing using the offset input. Compare with preset thresholds, which are editable and carry their status. Return a pair matrix and a list of closest pairs with coordinates. Approved-not-built towers are drawn with a hatched outline to show uncertain form.
visualization: Plan with separation lines coloured green (meets), red (below), amber (unverified threshold) and distances labelled
Elevation strip showing sky corridors between towers by level band
Floor-plate area bar chart by level with the team band shaded
Context towers coloured by status: existing, approved, proposed
outputs: separation_matrix: pair x band distances, m
modules.human_judgment: Judging tower rhythm, views between towers and urban-design quality; deciding to depart from a guideline; anticipating the final form of approved neighbours.
modules.limits: No City guideline PDF on tower separation or floor plate could be opened; 24.4 m is a recalled candidate only. Approved-but-unbuilt towers may change. Shadow, wind and daylight consequences belong to the CLIM packets.

modules.name: Program and FSR accounting
modules.design_question: How much floor area counts toward total FSR and the 9.0 non-residential minimum under gross and Vancouver-style net accounting, and how sensitive is compliance to exclusions and use classification?
inputs: Layer0 program-tagged slab polygons by level (or IFC spaces or mesh volumes)
Site area (gross, optionally net of dedications)
Exclusion preset (editable list with clause ids)
Use-classification switch (strict or broad)

parameters.name: Accounting basis (gross vs zoning floor area)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; zoning area subtracts listed exclusions, so FSR goes down. The brief's own basis is unstated, so both ledgers are shown.

parameters.name: Exclusion rules (example set)
parameters.relationship: Each enabled exclusion -> counted area down -> FSR down. Examples in CD-1 by-laws: parking, loading, mechanical at or below base surface; balconies to 8%; amenity to 1,000 m2; storage 3.7 m2 per unit; wall over 152 mm.

parameters.name: Use classification for the 9.0 minimum
parameters.relationship: Counting hotel, cultural/civic and public-oriented space raises non-residential FSR without changing the design. The brief says 'office, commercial'.

parameters.name: Site-area basis
parameters.relationship: Site area down (for example after dedications) -> FSR up for the same floor area. The brief gives only a gross block size.

parameters.name: Mechanical and core allocation
parameters.relationship: Mechanical floors up -> gross area and tower height up; whether they count toward FSR depends on the exclusion preset.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, strict
metrics.method: Office + commercial/retail area / site area.
metrics.basis: Brief minimum 9.0 non-residential, high-employment area.

metrics.name: Interpretation gap (broad minus strict)
metrics.good: gap does not change pass/fail
metrics.bad: strict < 9.0 <= broad: result depends on interpretation
metrics.method: Two classifications run side by side.
metrics.basis: Wording gap in the brief; ask Buildner.

metrics.name: Total FSR (all uses)
metrics.good: reported only; no overall cap in the brief
metrics.method: All counted area / site area; compare with Bay Parkade 27.4 (press, consolidated site) for orientation.
metrics.basis: Brief states no overall FSR limit; press figure for the precedent.

metrics.name: Exclusion documentation
metrics.good: 100% of exclusions carry a clause id and status
metrics.method: Count documented / total.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work and sources.

modules.method: Per level and per tag, sum slab polygon areas (Shapely) or IfcSpace quantities (IfcOpenShell). Build two ledgers: gross (all enclosed floor area) and zoning (gross minus enabled exclusions, each with a clause id and status). Divide by site area. Compute non-residential FSR under strict (office plus commercial/retail) and broad (add hotel, cultural/civic, public, amenity) classifications. Run one-at-a-time sensitivity: toggle each exclusion and classification switch and record the FSR change. Reconcile: ledger total equals the sum of level totals; warn when slab area is untagged. Exclusion values from CD-1 by-laws are shown as 'unverified examples', never as Downtown District rules.
visualization: Stacked bar by level (y = floor, x = m2) coloured by program tag
Waterfall: gross GFA -> exclusions -> counted area -> non-residential
FSR gauge with the 9.0 line; strict and broad markers
Tornado chart of FSR change per switch
outputs: fsr_ledger: level x tag table, gross and zoning
modules.human_judgment: Classifying mixed or ambiguous spaces; choosing which interpretation to claim; defending exclusions to the jury; confirming wording with Buildner.
modules.limits: Vancouver's exclusion rules in the Zoning and Development By-law and DD schedule were not read (HTTP 403); CD-1 values are site-specific examples. Massing-stage areas are approximate; net areas need core and MEP presets from other packets. This is not a plan check.

modules.name: Public benefits, density bonus and CAC ledger
modules.design_question: What public benefits does the scheme give for the density and height it seeks, how do they map to Vancouver's statutory tools, and how do they compare with Bay Parkade?
inputs: gfa_by_tag from P01-M07 (public, cultural/civic, amenity areas)
Public-realm and plaza areas from Layer 0
List of non-floor benefits (transit entrance, free-access deck) with user values
departure_register from P01-M02 and zoning_envelope from P01-M03

parameters.name: Density above base
parameters.relationship: The Charter allows base density plus higher density when amenities or affordable units are provided, so more extra FSR requested -> more benefit expected.

parameters.name: Form of benefit (in-kind, cash CAC, DCL, ACC)
parameters.relationship: Council may accept money equal to estimated capital cost instead of in-kind conditions; DCLs fund parks, daycare and utilities; ACCs fund community centres, libraries, public squares. More in-kind -> less cash.

parameters.name: Free-access floor area given
parameters.relationship: Free-access area up -> benefit up, saleable area down. Bay Parkade secured free resident access to its observation deck by rezoning condition.

parameters.name: Height and density beyond policy
parameters.relationship: In the one precedent, towers above policy came with about $305 million in benefits including $20 million cash CAC. No formula relating height to benefit was found.

parameters.name: Plan-area contribution expectations
parameters.relationship: The Granville Street Plan (approved 4 Jun 2025) lists a development contribution expectations policy; if the block lies in or near the plan area its terms apply. Text not read.

parameters.name: Transit entrance and public plaza as benefits
parameters.relationship: Bay Parkade counted new street-level and underground station entrances and a plaza among benefits, so VTC's below-grade entrance can be logged as a benefit item.

metrics.name: Statutory-tool mapping completeness
metrics.good: 100% of benefit items mapped to in-kind, cash CAC, DCL or ACC
metrics.method: Count mapped / total.
metrics.basis: Vancouver Charter ss. 565.1, 565.13, 523D, 523E.

metrics.name: Public-benefit floor-area share
metrics.good: team sets a target (no sourced value)
metrics.method: Free-access public, civic and amenity GFA / total GFA.
metrics.basis: Team preset; no sourced threshold.

metrics.name: Bay Parkade benchmark panel
metrics.good: report only
metrics.method: Show cash CAC about $20 million, in-kind about $184 million, package about $305 million, 27.4 FSR consolidated.
metrics.basis: Staff figures as reported by Daily Hive; FSR from Storeys; press accounts disagree on storeys.

metrics.name: Jury linkage
metrics.good: every benefit tagged to a jury criterion
metrics.method: Count tagged / total.
metrics.basis: Team preset.

modules.method: Create a ledger of benefit items (name, type, area or value, free-access flag, tool, jury tag, source). Map each item to in-kind, cash CAC, DCL or ACC using the Charter definitions. Compute the public floor-area share from P01-M07 tags and add public-realm area from Layer 0. Show the Bay Parkade benchmark labelled as press and staff figures. An optional sandbox lets the user type land values to explore how a CAC share would change; it ships empty and is labelled team assumption. The module does not estimate the City's CAC, which is negotiated from a land-lift analysis.
visualization: Sankey from density above base to benefit items to statutory tools
Benchmark bars: scheme vs Bay Parkade for cash, in-kind and floor-area share (labelled unverified)
Matrix of benefit items against the four jury criteria
modules.human_judgment: What counts as a real public benefit; Indigenous and community partnership content (CULT packet); economic viability; negotiating the package.
modules.limits: Vancouver's CAC and density-bonus policy documents, current DCL rates and any Vancouver amenity cost charge by-law were not opened, so no rates or percentages are given. Whether a large-site rezoning policy applies to a block of about 1.15 ha is unknown. Precedent figures come from press.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge: Building Higher Downtown (competition page)
sources.extract: Registration closes 29 Oct 2026; Q&A deadline 3 Nov 2026; submissions 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London time; winners 26 Jan 2027; CAD 15,000 prizes; seven-member jury. Brief, site plans and 3D model are email-gated downloads, so site, height, FSR and board rules are not on the page.

sources.title: VTC full competition brief (gated PDF; facts as supplied in project context)
sources.publisher: Buildner with City of Vancouver and UBC SALA
sources.extract: Site about 79.2 x 144.8 m; towers 244-305 m; minimum 9.0 non-residential FSR; no overall FSR limit; below-grade transit entrance; jury weights 40/30/20/10; policy reflection deliverable. Not independently opened in this run.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review (project page)
sources.extract: Policy adopted 1997. Phases: early directions (spring-summer 2026), draft policies (fall 2026-winter 2027), final policy (winter-spring 2027), hearing and adoption (spring 2027). Protected public views will not be reviewed or updated. Competition closes 30 Nov 2026.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review FAQ
sources.extract: Only minor height changes since 2011; competition will not set policy; Bay Parkade lies outside the current policy area, sites across the street inside it may consider up to 600 ft; Council 2023 direction sends non-conforming projects through rezoning.

sources.title: Memo: Higher Buildings Policy Review and public engagement (2 Apr 2026)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; listed in search results only.

sources.title: News release: Help shape tall buildings (May 2026)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: last comprehensive review 2011, tied to Granville Street Plan 2025, protected views not reviewed.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy for rezonings (current PDF)
sources.extract: HTTP 403. Named in the brief; text not read.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy, July 2018 version (H005)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: tallest buildings about 550-700 ft in the CBD; Queen Elizabeth view corridor is a trigger; enhanced review incl. Urban Design Panel.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy, 1 Feb 2011 version (H005_2011Feb01)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: adopted 1997; Figure 1 site map; about 700 ft on Georgia, Burrard or Granville; about 500 and 425 ft at bridgeheads.

sources.title: Council report and memo on Higher Buildings (20 Jan 2011)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: aim to add capacity without penetrating protected views.

sources.title: Urban Design Panel minutes, 26 Aug 2020
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: a 469 ft proposal in the Queen Elizabeth cone where the cone crosses the site at 332 ft triggers the Higher Buildings Policy.

sources.title: Public Views Guidelines (replaced View Protection Guidelines, 10 Jul 2024)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: view = origin point, cone(s), subject(s); cone has two vertical bounds and a lower boundary giving maximum geodetic height; buildings should lie outside cones; VanMap and open data hold cone geometry.

sources.title: Protecting public views (City page)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: Council replaced the guidelines on 10 Jul 2024; select Higher Buildings sites may enter Queen Elizabeth Park cone boundaries through a special review.

sources.title: Vancouver view cones policy change
sources.extract: Approved 10 Jul 2024; 38 cones from 18 origins cut to 24 (14 and 2 origins removed); 11 updated, 13 retained; Queen Elizabeth 3.1 and 3.2.4a eliminated, 3.2.1-3.2.4 retained; no height figures.

sources.title: Protected views Vancouver (4 Jul 2024)
sources.extract: Staff report recommended lowering the bottom of the Queen Elizabeth Park cone, opening over a million sq ft of floor space; cones have shaped policy since 1989.

sources.title: Opinion: Arbitrary view cone height restrictions are strangling Vancouver's potential
sources.extract: Six cones originate at the Queen Elizabeth Park peak; cones keep many downtown-adjacent sites to about 20-30 storeys; opinion, no height limits.

sources.title: Preliminary view cone calculation, 1070 Barclay St
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: cone 3.2.1 maximum geodetic elevations about 123-143 m at that West End site.

sources.title: Council report, Wall Centre site (6 Feb 1997)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: 1989 Queen Elizabeth corridor set 322.8 ft at the site, relaxable to 450 ft. Historical, superseded.

sources.title: Council staff presentation (5 Jul 2022), West End rezoning
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: view 3.2.1 at 361 ft for that site.

sources.title: Open data catalogue: View cones (archive record, Jan 2020)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: archived 2020 and 2015 snapshots exist; pre-2024 geometry.

sources.title: Updating Vancouver International Airport Zoning Regulations (consultation)
sources.extract: Proposes new height limits in Vancouver and Burnaby; new area covers much of Vancouver north of the Fraser to English Bay; consultation 14 Jul-12 Sep 2026, closed; no surface heights; parcel limits via aviation.pac@tc.gc.ca.

sources.title: Canada Gazette Part I, vol. 158, no. 17: Vancouver International Airport Zoning Regulations
sources.extract: Read first 100,000 of 129,740 characters. Outer surface 45 m above the reference point; approach 1:50 to 15 km; transitional 1:7; existing taller buildings may remain but not be raised; bump-out areas for taller buildings.

sources.title: Vancouver International Airport Zoning Regulations (SOR/80-902)
sources.extract: s.5 bars structures above approach, outer or transitional surfaces; approach 1:50 with 15% divergence to 15,000 m; outer plane 45 m above reference point (reference at 2 m); transitional 1:7; outer limits described mainly in Richmond.

sources.title: Standard 325 - Heliports (Canadian Aviation Regulations)
sources.extract: Read first 100,000 of 151,763 characters. Table 4-1 non-instrument approach surfaces: 245 m at 6-10%, then 830 m at 16%; transitional 50% to 45 m; H1 heliports use a critical-obstacle line and five-year survey.

sources.title: Land Use Program (NAV CANADA)
sources.extract: Assesses land use proposals near airports and air navigation infrastructure; portal submission since Aug 2025; reply usually 8-12 weeks, 12-18 months near airports; letter is not a permit.

sources.title: Vancouver Harbour Control Tower
sources.extract: Tower on Granville Square serves Vancouver Harbour Water Airport (CYHC); floating heliport to the east; busy floatplane and helicopter operations. No airspace limits given.

sources.title: Holborn Bay Parkade towers and NAV CANADA aviation constraint
sources.extract: NAV CANADA said design changes may be needed; possible cut of about 88 ft (27 m) from the 1,034 ft (315 m) tower to 946 ft (288 m); rezoning sets only a maximum height; YVR raised crane concerns at Oakridge.

sources.title: Holborn tallest tower, Bay Parkade redevelopment approved
sources.extract: Approved 27 Jul 2026, 7-3; cash CAC $20 million, in-kind social housing about $184 million, package about $305 million; free resident access to observation deck; new station entrances; delay motion rejected.

sources.title: Holborn supertall council approved
sources.extract: Consolidated site 27.4 FSR (original 31.29); three towers; storey counts differ from Daily Hive; aviation constraints unresolved.

sources.title: City council approves Vancouver's tallest tower project
sources.extract: Block bounded by Georgia, Seymour, Dunsmuir, Richards; 79-storey hotel and two 68-storey residential towers (conflicts with Daily Hive); NAV CANADA may require shorter towers.

sources.title: Vancouver Charter, Part XXVII (zoning, density benefits, ODPs)
sources.extract: Read first 100,000 of 115,510 characters. s.565.1 base plus higher density for amenities or affordable units; s.565.13 payment in place of conditions equals estimated capital cost; ss.565.11-565.16 consultation, feasibility analysis, reporting; s.563 effect of ODP.

sources.title: Vancouver Charter, Part XXIV-A (development cost levies)
sources.extract: s.523D: DCLs fund sewer, water, drainage, fire, police, highways, solid waste, parks and daycare; payable as a building-permit condition; not a percentage of construction cost.

sources.title: Vancouver Charter, Part XXIV-B (amenity cost charges)
sources.extract: ss.523E-523R: amenities include community, youth and seniors' centres, recreation, libraries, public squares; charge by lot, unit or m2; in-kind provision allowed; not charged where a DCL applies.

sources.title: Downtown Official Development Plan (DD.pdf)
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summary: regulates land use, minimum and maximum FSR, parking caps and loading minimums; height and amenities are interpretive; Development Permit Board may relax for hardship.

sources.title: CD-1 by-laws used as FSR-exclusion examples (CD-1 (254), (287), (318), (323), (331), (503))
sources.extract: HTTP 403; search summaries: parking, loading, mechanical at or below base surface excluded; balconies up to 8%; amenity up to 1,000 m2 or a share; storage 3.7 m2 per unit; wall allowance 152 mm. Site-specific.

sources.title: Granville Street Plan (project page)
sources.extract: Approved 4 Jun 2025 with a rezoning policy and Special Design District Guidelines; a development contribution expectations policy is listed; no heights or FSR on the page.

sources.title: Criteria for defining and measuring tall buildings
sources.extract: Height to architectural top (antennae excluded), to highest occupied floor, to tip; all measured from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance; supertall 300 m; storey-counting rules.

flags.claim: The View Protection Guidelines are the governing view policy.
flags.correction: Council replaced them with the Public Views Guidelines on 10 Jul 2024: 38 cones cut to 24, view 3.1 removed, 3.2.1-3.2.4 retained. Use post-2024 geometry.
flags.detail: Confirmed by Storeys (opened); the City page is unopened. The scope text and older council documents still use the old name.

flags.claim: YVR airport zoning caps downtown tower heights.
flags.detail: Current SOR/80-902 outer limits are described mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary; no source says downtown is inside. Transport Canada's July 2026 proposal covers much of Vancouver north of the Fraser, but surface heights are unpublished. Bay Parkade's NAV CANADA issue shows aviation can still cut height.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy height range is about 550-700 ft in the CBD.
flags.detail: From search summaries of the 2011 and 2018 versions; the City FAQ (opened) says up to 600 ft for the policy-area sites near Bay Parkade. Read the current PDF. Adoption date also differs between summaries (22 Apr vs 6 May 1997); amendments cited: 2003, 2011, 2018.

flags.claim: Do hotel, cultural/civic and public-oriented floor area count toward the 9.0 non-residential minimum?
flags.detail: Brief says 'office, commercial'. P01-M01 and P01-M07 show strict and broad results. Ask Buildner before the Q&A closes on 3 Nov 2026; registration closes 29 Oct 2026.

flags.claim: Which height measure and which towers must lie inside 244-305 m?
flags.detail: Brief wording is 'one or more towers in the range'. Default is strict: every tower, architectural-top measure. Put the question to Buildner by 3 Nov 2026.

flags.claim: Downtown tower separation is 24.4 m (80 ft) and residential floor plates are capped near 6,500 sq ft.
flags.detail: Recalled from Downtown South guidelines, not found or opened in this run (search quota ran out). Shown only as an editable candidate in P01-M06.

flags.claim: Queen Elizabeth cone floors near downtown are about 100-145 m geodetic.
flags.detail: Derived from older documents: 322.8 ft (1997, 1989 cones), 361 ft (2022), 332 ft (2020), and 123-143 m (1070 Barclay); all unopened and pre-2024 or site-specific. Use the City's current cone data.

flags.claim: Bay Parkade tower heights and storeys.
flags.detail: Daily Hive says the hotel is 68 storeys / 315 m and a residential tower 79 storeys; Construction Canada says the hotel is 79 storeys. FSR 27.4 comes from Storeys only. Use as a precedent range only.

flags.claim: Where is the hypothetical block, and what vertical datum do cone elevations use?
flags.detail: Cone, zoning, ODP sub-area and airspace results all depend on an assumed real location and datum (geodetic vs CGVD2013 not confirmed). The team must fix one assumption and record it.

flags.claim: Do the City's rezoning policies for large sites, the CAC policy and the Metro Core jobs policy apply to a block of about 1.15 ha?
flags.detail: Not researched: City hosts blocked and search quota ran out. Also unknown whether VTC's 9.0 non-residential minimum mirrors an ODP or Metro Core rule.

flags.claim: Default rule readings (strict tower band, public-use level bands, review freshness, precedent flag at 288 m).
flags.detail: Presets are editable and shown in the team-assumption colour until a source replaces them.

unresolved_relationships: Acceptable occlusion of the North Shore mountain skyline from Queen Elizabeth Park versus tower angular width: no sourced threshold found.
Relationship between tower height or density beyond policy and the size of the CAC or benefits package: only one precedent (Bay Parkade), no formula.
Allowable tower height versus distance under Transport Canada's proposed 2026 zoning surfaces over downtown: surfaces unpublished.
Relationship between floor-plate width and required tower separation in downtown guidelines: no sourced relationship found.
Which uses count toward the VTC 9.0 non-residential FSR and how exclusions apply to that count: brief wording and DD schedule not confirmed.
Skew angle between the downtown street grid and true north for the brief's site plan: value not obtained.
Whether Higher Buildings Policy review drafts will raise heights or change tower design criteria: drafts not public until early 2027.

R1: Added the Bay Parkade rezoning (27 Jul 2026) as a live precedent for height beyond policy, aviation risk and benefits.
R1: Recorded the 2026 review timeline (draft policies fall 2026-winter 2027; hearing spring 2027) and that protected views are outside the review.
